analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: a date stamp, the SDK 27 release-qualification description (lines ~996-1004), a new test script entry (line 1295), and a cluster-runtime release-test description (lines ~1331-1346, 1359-1362). I examined both head-text units in full. No executable code, workflow, key handling, wire contract or cache-storage logic changes in the supplied evidence, so no threat-model control (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, TB-012, T-041, T-053 etc.) is weakened by this diff.

Security-relevant claims in the docs: (1) sharded qualify-sdk jobs run on separate Macs, a final `qualify-sdk` job audits executed counts per shard against the full suite list, and signing requires `qualify-sdk` plus optimized compilation. This describes a stronger or equal gate; the actual workflow (.github/workflows, scripts/provider-test-shards.py) was not supplied, so the implementation of the count audit and signing dependency is unverified. (2) The cluster runtime release rows (`cluster_runtime` block, registration body limit, no-secret facts step with keychain removed first) describe release/registration behavior owned by scripts and workflows outside this batch. If those files change in the same PR, the next pass should check that registration sends the block canonically, the 64 KiB limit refuses before staging, and that `provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh` is handled without secrets, since A-011/A-017 release registration depends on them. Documentation drift alone is not a finding. Unit text of the first doc appears truncated at 1381, and the patch excerpt is incomplete; the remaining content was not visible, which is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
